Museum of Science, Boston
www.mos.org
Innovation and creativity come from the unique perspectives of a diverse staff.  We value your perspective.
Who We Are
As science and technology increasingly shape our lives, the Museum of Science strives to equip and inspire everyone to use science for the global good while keeping up with the pace of change. Among the world’s largest science centers and New England’s most attended cultural institution, we engage nearly five million people a year – at Science Park and in museums around the world, in classrooms, and online.
The Museum’s singular location connecting Boston and Cambridge puts us at the junction of some of the world’s most influential academic institutions and industries, local and state government, schools, and the public. Trusted by each sector, we are ideally positioned to convene, inspire, and create meaningful experiences for all. Come join us on our mission to inspire a lifelong love of science in everyone and living our vision for a world where science belongs to each of us for the good of all of us.
Why We Need You
The Museum's websites are how millions of people each year plan a visit, buy tickets, become members, donate, and explore science online. The Full Stack Developer owns the user-facing side of that experience: making thoughtful UX/UI decisions, building polished and accessible interfaces, and writing the server-side code and API integrations that make them work — connecting our sites to the ticketing, CRM, and payment systems behind every transaction.
You'll partner closely with our Lead Web Developer on a small, high-trust team where your work ships to production and reaches real visitors quickly. You'll bring genuine design judgment, care about getting the details right, and use AI development tools fluently as part of everyday coding, review, and research. Our properties run on Drupal hosted on Acquia, so CMS experience helps — but we are hiring a strong web developer first and will teach the platform.
What You’ll Accomplish
User-facing feature delivery: Design, build, test, and ship user-facing features for the Museum's web properties — polished, accessible interfaces backed by the server-side code and API calls they need — taking ownership from problem definition through production deployment.
UX/UI design ownership: Lead user experience and interface decisions for the web team: translate loosely defined needs into wireframes, prototypes, and polished, accessible (WCAG-conformant) interfaces, and build toward a reusable component/design system so the team no longer depends on other departments for UX/UI direction.
API integration: Build and maintain the connections between the Museum's websites and business-critical systems — including Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Ticketure ticketing, and payment/commerce services — consuming REST/JSON APIs and writing the server-side code that keeps transactional workflows like ticket purchase and membership registration reliable.
Quality and craft: Verify your work thoroughly before handoff — across browsers, devices, and assistive technology — and catch the edge cases, not just the happy path. Where it adds value, contribute automated tests to the codebases we depend on most.
AI-assisted engineering: Use LLM-based development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot and similar) as an integral part of coding, code review, debugging, and technical research, while applying the judgment to verify and validate AI-assisted output; contribute to the team's evolving standards for effective and responsible AI-assisted development.
Codebase modernization and refactoring: Assess inherited and legacy codebases, plan incremental refactors, and execute them safely — reducing technical debt, improving structure and performance, and leaving the systems you touch easier to maintain than you found them.
Timely research and solution design: Take ambiguous technical problems, run timeboxed investigations, and deliver clear, actionable recommendations (proofs of concept, architecture decision records) that move from question to working solution on a predictable timeline.
Platform contribution: Contribute to the delivery work on the Museum's CMS-based properties (currently Drupal on Acquia) — component development, security updates, and releases within the team's Git, DDEV, and CI/CD workflows — in partnership with the Lead Web Developer, who provides technical leadership for the team.
Perform other work-related duties as required by Manager.
This is a HYBRID position, requiring at least one day per week working onsite at the Museum of Science in Boston.
What We’re Looking For (Competencies)
Technical chops — a frontend-forward developer: You bring 3+ years of professional web development experience with deep frontend expertise: semantic HTML, expert-level CSS/SASS, and strong modern JavaScript, including a framework such as React. Behind the interface, you're comfortable writing server-side code (PHP or Node) and calling APIs to power your features — you don't need to be a backend specialist, but you never need someone else to wire up an endpoint for you.
A UX/UI practitioner: You have real experience making design decisions, not just implementing someone else's mockups: information architecture, interaction patterns, responsive layout, and accessibility. You can show interfaces you shaped and explain the reasoning. This matters here because the web team owns the UX/UI decisions for our properties.
An API integrator: You have consumed REST/JSON APIs to connect websites to external systems (CRMs, payment or ticketing platforms, marketing systems), and you understand authentication and error handling in transactional workflows. Our sites are the front door to Salesforce- and Ticketure-backed business processes.
High standards — you check your own work: You verify before you hand off: cross-browser, responsive, accessible, and edge cases included. You'd rather find the problem yourself than have it found in review or in production, and you report status accurately — including what you have and haven't tested.
AI-fluent development: You use LLM coding assistants effectively in daily work — for generation, review, and research — and, critically, you know how to validate what they produce. AI tooling is integral to how this team develops and reviews code, and we need someone who amplifies their judgment with it rather than substituting it.
Analytical skills — research to recommendation: You can take an open-ended technical question, structure an investigation, and deliver a clear recommendation with evidence on a committed timeline. On a small team, investigation work can't stall; we need someone who reliably converts ambiguity into decisions.
Accountability and follow-through: You do what you say you will, and you raise blockers early instead of working in isolation. Trust on a small team is built on precise, honest communication about the state of the work.
Curiosity and learning — growth mindset: You actively close your own skill gaps, absorb feedback, and apply it in the next piece of work. Our stack and tooling evolve quickly, and the role rewards people who enjoy that.
Collaboration on a small team: You work fluently in Git (branching, merging, resolving conflicts independently), participate constructively in code review in both directions, and communicate clearly in agile ceremonies with technical and non-technical partners alike.
Preferred: Any of these will shorten your ramp or expand what you can take on, and none are required: hands-on experience with Drupal or WordPress (theming, module/plugin development, site building); experience writing automated unit or integration tests (PHPUnit, Jest/Vitest) and wiring them into CI; TypeScript; or design-tool fluency (Figma).
A flexible, local partner: You reside within commuting distance of Boston. We offer a highly flexible hybrid schedule that pivots with project needs, and you're ready to be on-site at the Museum when the work calls for it — planning sessions, rapid troubleshooting, or team events.
How We Work-Our Values
Mission-Focused: We inspire a lifelong love of science in everyone.
Audience-Driven: Everything we do begins with the people we serve.
Innovative: We are curious, take smart risks, share responsibility, and own outcomes.
Generous: We offer time and energy towards common goals.

About Goodfire
Goodfire is an AI interpretability research lab. We build interpretability agents and infrastructure to understand, monitor, and align AI models.
We believe that AI is the most consequential technology of our time. Yet AI models are trained by trial and error today, with limited understanding of what drives their behavior. Our goal is to advance the research and technology needed to fully understand and align AI so humanity can trust superintelligence.
Goodfire is a public benefit corporation founded by researchers who helped pioneer the field of interpretability at OpenAI and Google DeepMind. We are headquartered in San Francisco and have raised over $200M from leading investors including Lightspeed, Menlo, and B Capital.
About the role
We’re looking for a Forward Deployed Research Scientist to join our team to work directly with customers to apply our interpretability platform to solve novel problems for our customers. You’ll work closely with a small, mission-driven team of scientists and engineers to conduct novel research, build practical tools, and push the field forward.
Where you might contribute:
Forward deployed research – lead research with our partners to interpret advanced models.
Project delivery and implementation – own research delivery on high-stakes projects with customers and do whatever it takes to make delivery successful, including: problem and hypothesis definition, data sourcing, tool building, iteration, and implementation. Translate research into tools for real-world applications.
Key Responsibilities:
Work directly with customers to conduct original research in interpretability.
Prototype techniques to visualize and manipulate internal model structures.
Collaborate with engineering to turn research into production-ready tools.
Drive partnership success by collaborating closely with our customers and partners.
Help define and evolve our research direction.
What you’ll bring
Required experience
MS/PhD or equivalent experience in CS, with a strong ML background and experience in interpretability.
Deep familiarity with large models and a passion for understanding how they work.
Fluency in Python and ML frameworks such as PyTorch.
Strong writing and communication skills for explaining complex ideas.
Drive to move quickly and take ownership.
Preferred qualifications
Experience leading research in a forward deployed environment and in service of a customer’s requirements.
Experience in startup or fast-paced lab environments.
Our values
Goodfire is looking for individuals who embody our values and share our deep commitment to making interpretability accessible. We are building a team first and foremost.
Put mission and team first
All we do is in service of our mission. We trust each other, deeply care about the success of the organization, and choose to put our team above ourselves.
Improve constantly
We are constantly looking to improve every piece of the business. We proactively critique ourselves and others in a kind and thoughtful way that translates to practical improvements in the organization. We are pragmatic and consistently implement the obvious fixes that work.
Take ownership and initiative
There are no bystanders here. We proactively identify problems and take full responsibility over getting a strong result. We are self-driven, own our mistakes, and feel deep responsibility over what we’re building.
Action today
We have a small amount of time to do something incredibly hard and meaningful. The pace and intensity of the organization is high. If we can take action today or tomorrow, we will choose to do it today.
Where we work
We are hiring for this position in our San Francisco HQ. We are in person 5 days a week, with one company-wide remote week per month.
What we offer
This role offers market competitive salary, equity, and competitive benefits.
The expected salary range for this position is $220,000 - $315,000 USD
Most importantly, you'll have the opportunity to join a vital mission at an important point in its trajectory — we are developing groundbreaking technology with a world-class team on the critical path to ensuring a safe and beneficial future for humanity. If you want to do your life’s work with us, even if you believe you do not meet every single requirement, apply now.
